notes.description: Descriptive statistics and correlation helpers depend on exact sample-size conventions, divisor choices, and bias flags. Small implementation changes can silently shift results while still looking numerically plausible.
notes.mitigation: Keep fixture-derived parity gates at the function level and preserve explicit per-case tolerances instead of collapsing everything to a single suite-wide threshold.

notes.description: Rank-based and goodness-of-fit tests are sensitive to sample ordering, ties, and tail behavior. Regressions often appear first in p-values rather than headline statistics.
notes.mitigation: Track both statistic and p-value parity in the evidence bundle and keep edge-case fixtures for tied, monotone, and boundary-distribution samples.

notes.description: Utilities like z-score normalization and entropy can degrade under degenerate or nearly degenerate inputs, producing NaNs or masking divide-by-zero behavior.
notes.mitigation: Retain differential fixtures that cover narrow spreads and probability-style inputs, and fail the evidence pack if any previously finite path starts emitting non-finite outputs.
